title: The seven classifier disagreements include a two-token page and aggregated foldout panels; audit the published feature pipeline
statement: Partial source audit for K-045-open-1, not a blind palaeographic classification. The paper https://ceur-ws.org/Vol-3313/paper5.pdf links a public folder https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1extY_zleORyb1t4sYY9WA7bzchlCH5d6. Downloaded from that folder, zl.txt SHA-256 a21d79f0da44a4e159dbb6f5656a7e1071366f8dec629973834671d73e0a2ef9, voynich.ipynb SHA-256 7231ce66c0e8ba4e60b23dcfec427817cab3143f40ea2efbeeeeffb8348e7ac8, and results.csv SHA-256 8f8918fa11b0e7aeca01b707c15404c00d7e052fb2df86d060264c3726e186d7. The CSV has 93 nonempty labeled rows (31 per reported scribe) and confirms the seven unanimously disagreeing trigram rows listed by the paper. Applying the released notebook's prefix matching and preprocessing to its input yields f57v 178 tokens; f65v 37; f85r 457 from f85r1 316 and f85r2 141; f86v 1239 from f86v4 168, f86v6 444, f86v5 366 and f86v3 261; f95r 170 from f95r1 94 and f95r2 76; f95v 166 from f95v2 57 and f95v1 109; and f116v just two ('oror', 'sheey'). Thus published foldout identifiers are pooled text inputs, not single ZL panel identifiers. The paper itself cautions about low counts. In the released notebook, featureMatrixGenerator calls featureMatrixNormaliser first on training and then on test data; that helper calls vec.fit_transform each time. Even with a fixed vocabulary and training min/max, this refits TF-IDF IDF on each test fold instead of applying the training-fitted IDF. This uses unlabeled test-fold text, not test labels, and we have not measured its impact or established that this exact notebook revision produced the CSV. The described results do not demonstrate classifier error or a hand reassignment. Yale's f116v canvas 1006277 shows sparse mixed-script writing; the published two-token text gives particularly little material for a blind same-glyph handwriting comparison. No blind matched image-feature assessment has yet been done.
check: Independently verify the seven CSV predictions and prefix-based token counts from the linked files and their hashes. Reproduce the published fold construction and compare stored-training-IDF transform against refitted-test-IDF on identical folds, reporting page-level predictions, vocabulary and seed differences. Before any blinded image judgment, map each pooled foldout input to exact IIIF canvases, prespecify same-glyph and same-layout controls, and require a minimum number of usable exemplars; mark f116v unassessable if it cannot meet that minimum. Compare at least two independent blinded readers and report disagreements rather than assigning a hand from the trigram labels.
